attempts.prompt:
Use case: compositing. Create one high-resolution portrait-card fusion using exactly two inputs. Image1 original small card is the sole authority for clothing, pose, hair, expression, light, and crop. Image2 provides mascot identity and anatomy only. Transform the human anatomy into a smooth golden-yellow compact near-round mascot head and body with green-ringed black eyes and a source-matching mouth. Preserve the actual bare head features: high receding hairline, very short close-cropped dark brown hair at top and sides, actual brow hair, thin restrained grey/dark upper-lip moustache, clean chin, and stern closed mouth. Fine primary eye-rim detail remains unresolved; keep it understated and do not invent prominent new glasses. Maintain the actual dark navy closed upright-collar naval tunic with small gold collar areas. Preserve the source-exposed gold/pale star-shaped chest fitting near lower center and the limited blue/gold cord and muted multicolor ribbon strip along bottom image-left beside the note. Do not omit this visible decoration region or invent large areas hidden by the note. Ensure the rounded chin immediately meets the raised/broadened existing neckline with a very short broad neck transition and minimal throat exposure. No separate yellow neck shaft, pointed V funnel, pinched collar, neck rolls, floating collar, clipping, or cream belly bib. Preserve actual open/closed garment and fastening with coherent front/rear collar overlap and contact shadow. Retain the complete tilted dark frame, opaque photographic backing in its actual source color, and the attached lower-right cream note with faint indistinct upper marks and actual overlap. All solid surfaces must be opaque, with alpha only outside the complete card silhouette. No invented insignia, text, or accessories.
FINAL EXACT SOURCE REQUIREMENT: BAREHEADED nearly frontal/angled naval bust with high receding hairline and very short close-cropped DARK/BROWN hair at top/sides, actual brow HAIR, thin restrained GREY/DARK upper-lip MOUSTACHE and clean chin, stern CLOSED mouth. Fine eye-rim shading in primary is unresolved, do not invent prominent new glasses. Actual DARK NAVY CLOSED upright-collar naval tunic with small GOLD collar areas. Preserve source-exposed GOLD/PALE star-shaped chest fitting near lower center and limited BLUE/GOLD cord and muted multicolor ribbon strip along bottom IMAGE-LEFT beside note. Do not omit this visible decoration region or invent the large areas hidden by note. No white shirt, tie, open business lapels or new chin beard.
Retain exact primary head angle, expression, cap shape, real hair and visible clothing/decoration areas. One compact near-round yellow mascot head with a clearly ROUNDED short chin immediately contacting raised broad collar, no V-shaped lower-face funnel or yellow shaft. Do not copy human long neck or angular jaw into mascot anatomy; fit the original neckline around the compact rounded head. Preserve actual dark solid cloth and photographic backing opacity. Tiny ambiguous features remain understated; no new badge engraving or decorations hidden behind note. Image1 exact original card; Image2 mascot identity/anatomy only.
Output alpha: genuine transparent RGBA ONLY OUTSIDE the complete original framed portrait silhouette. The photographic BACKING INSIDE the frame is a required OPAQUE surface: preserve its original background color and texture behind the character all the way to the inner frame rim. Never turn the gaps between frame and character into transparent holes or a window. Keep the actual frame angle and rim. Preserve an overlapping paper note, pin or other attachment ONLY when actually visible in this exact source; otherwise do not invent one. Do not invent a new backdrop outside the whole card. Retain source clothing, hair, headgear, lighting and crop at full generated resolution. All originally OPAQUE subject surfaces must remain FULLY OPAQUE (alpha 255): yellow head/body, hair, beard, dark or black clothing, coat lapels, collar, tie, buttons and decorations. Dark cloth is colored material, not transparent background. Never fade garment interiors into semi-transparent patches, holes, white haze or see-through fabric. Keep any genuine source outer-edge alpha falloff only at that actual exterior boundary; preserve actual source transparency rather than making the subject itself translucent.
